description: Ledger of cell families that a registered apply_patch write targets while no registered write produces a base value for them. An apply_patch needs a base, and event-auth-state-resolution.md section 9.3.1.2 forbids closing the gap with a registered initial_value: the base must come from a registered create or genesis write. Opened 2026-09-07 with four entries by review/spec-open/2026-09-07-1305-four-apply-patch-targets-have-no-registered-producer.md and emptied the same day by decisions/0029. families_without_base_producer only shrinks; a new entry is a defect, not a baseline update. resolved_families is kept as the record of what each fix was.

resolved_families.note: control-plane cas_register; its settled value is null until the first patch, so the object's truth is defined by an update rather than by a create. Highest priority of the four.
resolved_families.resolution: ak.circle.create now sets payload.object on id:circle(envelope.event_id), atomically with the existing create-log and history-access effects.

resolved_families.note: ak.strand.create writes ak.component.strand.object.v1 instead, so create and update land on different families.
resolved_families.resolution: family retired; ak.strand.update patches ak.component.strand.object.v1, which ak.strand.create sets.

resolved_families.note: no create or genesis writer registers a base for the tracks subtree.
resolved_families.resolution: family retired; ak.strand.tracks.update patches ak.component.strand.object.v1 for the same reason.

resolved_families.note: ak.view.create writes ak.component.view.create.v1 and ak.view.reconcile a third family; the update and reconcile subjects are also a bare string rather than id:view.
resolved_families.resolution: family retired; create, update and reconcile all address ak.component.view.v1 with an id:view subject.
